clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today with fat-based grading of carcasses, and what decision would real-time data on each carcass drive?
clarification_questions.why: Clarifies the business problem and whether inline grading per carcass is the right decision support.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Current grading pain unknown; the first step is to define the decision the real-time data must support.

clarification_questions.question: Which exact variable defines fat content (total fat, lipid fraction, or a specific fat-related analyte), and what concentration range is relevant?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether the target is a major component (percent level) or a trace analyte, which governs method choice.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Target definition and level unknown; lab screening establishes whether it is a major or trace component.

clarification_questions.question: In what state do the carcasses reach the measurement point: surface condition, skin presence, moisture, and is the surface opaque or wet?
clarification_questions.why: ATR needs intimate contact with a defined surface; surface condition decides whether contact-based MIR is feasible at all.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Surface condition unknown; ATR contact feasibility is not established.

clarification_questions.question: Can the probe touch the carcass, and what cleaning, hygiene or sterilization regime applies to the line?
clarification_questions.why: Contact and cleaning requirements decide whether an ATR probe is usable and how it must be built.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Contact and hygiene conditions unknown; a non-contact option may be needed.

clarification_questions.question: What is the planned distance between the probe and the carcass, the conveyor speed, and the carcass-to-carcass variability in size and shape?
clarification_questions.why: Distance and motion determine signal quality and whether the probe can see the same spot consistently.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Distance and motion unknown; mounting geometry is not yet defined.

clarification_questions.question: What reference method is used today to determine carcass fat content, and what accuracy does it achieve?
clarification_questions.why: Any optical method must be compared against the existing reference to judge whether it is accurate enough.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method and its accuracy unknown; comparison design cannot be fixed yet.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required, and which standards or customer specifications must the grading meet before results are shared as validated?
clarification_questions.why: Defines acceptance criteria and clarifies what validation means for customer communication.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; no validation claim can be made until criteria and a lab comparison exist.

flags_before_revision.detail: different_context: The cited S01 p.17 text says inline NIR reflection is used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products (yogurt, butter, whole milk concentrates), and its fat example is milk fat and protein. The claim presents this as the AFS example for fat in opaque food products and transfers it to carcasses without saying so. Only the contact-free point is supported by S01 p.10. Fix: Quote the dairy context explicitly: S01 p.17 describes inline NIR reflection for opaque dairy products (yogurt, butter, whole milk concentrates) and fat/protein in milk; state that carcass use is untested and needs its own validation, citing S01 p.10 for diffuse reflection at a distance.

not_supported: The cited pages do not say that fluorescence added no fat information. S04 p.4 only says IR works better for fat and fluorescence is well suited to liver, and that the concatenated model separated the classes. Fix: Remove the statement that fluorescence added no fat information, or state only that S04 p.4 reports IR as better than fluorescence for fat discrimination in the chicken model.

not_supported: None of the cited table rows or pages state that NIR diffuse reflection at a distance should be the primary interface, or that MIR ATR should serve only as a contact comparison. They give method characteristics, not a design decision for this application. Fix: Cite S01 p.10 for NIR diffuse reflectance at a distance and S01 p.10 for ATR probes needing contact with liquid or soft solid samples, and label the primary/comparison choice as an AFS design recommendation rather than a source finding.

not_supported: S01 p.10 covers ATR fiber probes, NIR chemometrics and instrumentation. It does not mention species, cut or feed changes or invalidation of matrix-specific calibration. Fix: Replace the citation with a page that discusses calibration transfer or matrix dependence, or mark the risk as an AFS engineering judgement not drawn from S01 p.10.

not_supported: S01 p.17 says NIR reflection is sensitive to surface characteristics and fat globule size. It does not mention moisture or temperature, or say these mimic fat changes. Fix: Limit the risk to surface characteristics and fat globule size as stated in S01 p.17, and add moisture and temperature only with a source page that supports them.

RAMAN.nominal_range: Raman shift in cm-1; signal recorded in the visible / short-wave NIR (400-1100 nm); state the laser excitation separately [S01 p.11]

FLUO.nominal_range: UV/Vis excitation and emission; depends on the fluorescent species [S01 p.12]

UVVIS.nominal_range: UV 190-360 nm and visible; depends on target and setup [S01 p.5]

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [guidance]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [guidance]
